To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cu supplementation increased the ileal digesta pH and decreased the Zn solu-bility and complex size in the duodena+jejunum contents.
Cu supplementation increased the pH of ileal contents but not the pH of gizzard contents.
high levels of dietary Cu supplementation increased pH of ileal digesta and antagonism between Zn and Cu in the digestive tract.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of Cu source and Cu supplementation on the solubilities of Ca, Cu, Zn, and their complex sizes in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT).
the effects of dietary Cu supplementation on the solubilities of Ca, Zn and Cu in the digesta and complex size of these minerals.
the effects of high levels of dietary Cu and Cu sources on the pH of the gastrointestinal tract and complex size of Cu, Ca, and Zn in the duodena + jejunum content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dietary Cu supplementation increased the pH of ileal contents and the portion of soluble Zn associated with large molecular complexes, whereas Cu lysinate decreased the solubility and small complex size of Zn in the duodeno-jejunal contents.
Cu supplementation increased ileal pH, and Cu supplementation or Cu source affected the Zn complex sizes, but did not affect the Ca complex sizes.
dietary Cu supplementation and Cu source did not affect Ca solubility and complex size in the duodena + jejunum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of high Cu supplementation and Cu source on pH and solubility of minerals in the digesta of the broiler chickens are minimal, and the antagonism of Cu on Zn is not related to pH of the digestive tract.
high Cu supplementation increased the pH of ileal contents, but the solubility and complex size of Cu and Zn were not altered.
Cu supplementation and Cu source have no effects on the pH of the digesta and the solubility or the complex size of Ca.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cu lysinate decreased Zn solubility, and Cu supplementation increased Zn complex size.

the Cu source and Cu supplementation did not affect the solubility and the complex size of Ca in the digesta, but the Cu source did affect the Zn solubilization and complex size in the digesta of broilers.

Cu supplementation increased the pH of ileal contents, which may affect the absorption of nutrients and minerals, and Cu supplementation and source had no effects of the pH of gizzard and duodenum + jejunal digesta.
